ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the diagonals AC and BD of rhombus ABCD intersect at point O. If $\angle BAC = 52^\circ$, then what is the measure of $\angle CDO$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus, \\
it follows that AD=CD, and $\angle CAD=\angle BAC=52^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle ADC=180^\circ - \angle CAD - \angle ACD=180^\circ - 52^\circ - 52^\circ=76^\circ$,\\
hence, $\angle CDO= \frac{1}{2}\angle ADC=\boxed{38^\circ}$.

From the text, use that ABCD is a rhombus and ∠BAC = 52°. Since AC is a diagonal of a rhombus, it bisects angle A, so ∠CAD = ∠BAC = 52°. In triangle ADC, AD = CD because all sides of a rhombus are equal, so the base angles at A and C are equal; hence ∠ACD = 52° and ∠ADC = 180° - 52° - 52° = 76°. Finally, diagonal BD bisects angle D in a rhombus, and O lies on BD in the image, so ∠CDO = 76°/2 = 38°.
